config.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters

intro.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a function that finds the length of the longest substring without any repeating characters in a given string. You will learn the sliding window technique, a core algorithmic pattern for efficiently processing sequential data. The main constructs involved are strings, sets or maps for tracking characters, and loops to traverse the input. This beginner-friendly lesson will help you understand how to solve common string manipulation problems step by step.
intro.usecase: The Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters algorithm is essential in text processing and validation, such as ensuring unique session IDs or detecting repeated patterns in user input. In real-world applications, it's used in search engines to analyze query strings for duplicate keywords, in code editors to highlight repeated variable names, and in data validation for forms to prevent duplicate entries in fields like usernames or serial numbers. This pattern helps maintain data integrity and optimize performance in systems handling large volumes of text.

objectives: Implement a sliding window algorithm to track unique characters in a string
Construct a character frequency map using JavaScript objects
Initialize and update window boundaries to maintain substring uniqueness
Manipulate the sliding window to expand and contract based on character repetition
Integrate conditional logic to detect and handle repeating characters
Configure a loop to iterate through the string and calculate maximum substring length
Apply the algorithm to solve the longest substring problem with test cases

content.body: Have you ever tried to find the longest sequence of unique letters in a word? That's exactly what we'll do today! We'll learn how to efficiently find the longest substring without repeating characters using a clever technique called the sliding window.
content.title: Let's begin

content.body:
1. Explain what a sliding window is in algorithm design.
2. Apply the expand/shrink logic to track unique characters.
3. Implement the longest substring algorithm in JavaScript.
4. Identify when to expand and shrink the window during execution.
content.title: What you'll learn

content.body: Let's start with a small example. Look at the string "abcabcbb". Can you find the longest sequence where no letter repeats? Try to trace it with your finger - start from the beginning and see how far you can go without hitting a duplicate character.
content.title: Try it

content.body: As you traced, you probably moved your finger along until you found a duplicate. What happened when you hit 'a' again after "abc"? Did you start over from the beginning, or did you adjust your starting point? Think about how you could keep going while maintaining only unique characters.
content.title: Think about the movement

content.body: You just experienced the core challenge: when you encounter a duplicate, you need to adjust your sequence. If you started over completely each time, that would be inefficient - like checking every possible substring from scratch.
content.title: What you did

content.body: Imagine a string with 10,000 characters. Checking every possible substring would be incredibly slow. We need a smarter way to move through the string without backtracking unnecessarily. Can't figure it out? Let me show you the approach on the next step.
content.title: Why it gets hard

content.body: Think of your sequence as a moving segment or 'window' across the string. The window expands to include new characters, but when we find a duplicate, we shrink it from the left side. This sliding window technique lets us efficiently track the longest unique sequence.
content.title: Key idea
content.visualMetaphor: Highlight a moving segment of the array; show expand and shrink.

content.body: Here's the better idea: We'll maintain a window using two pointers (left and right). As we move the right pointer to expand the window, we track characters we've seen. When we encounter a duplicate, we move the left pointer forward to shrink the window until all characters are unique again. We keep track of the maximum window size we've seen.
content.title: The approach

content.body:
1. Initialize left pointer at 0 and a Set to track characters
2. Move right pointer through the string
3. If character at right is not in Set, add it and update max length
4. If character is in Set, remove characters from left until duplicate is gone
5. Repeat until right reaches end of string
6. Return the maximum length found
content.title: Steps

steps.title: Set up the function
steps.instruction: Create the function skeleton with parameters and return statement. We'll call it lengthOfLongestSubstring and it should take a string s as input.
steps.hint: Start with function declaration and return 0 for now.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've set up the basic function structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: Almost there! Make sure you have the function name and parameter correct.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. We need a function called lengthOfLongestSubstring that takes a string parameter s.

steps.title: Initialize variables
steps.instruction: Inside the function, initialize the variables we'll need: left pointer at 0, maxLength at 0, and a Set to track characters.
steps.hint: Use let for variables and new Set() for the character tracker.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've set up the initial state for our sliding window.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Don't forget to initialize all three variables.
steps.feedbackWrong: We need left pointer, maxLength, and a Set. Try using: let left = 0; let maxLength = 0; let charSet = new Set();

steps.title: Set up the main loop
steps.instruction: Add a for loop to iterate through the string with the right pointer. We'll use right as our loop variable starting from 0.
steps.hint: Use a standard for loop: for (let right = 0; right < s.length; right++)
steps.feedbackCorrect: Excellent! The loop will let us expand our window to the right.
steps.feedbackPartial: Almost! Make sure your loop goes from 0 to s.length.
steps.feedbackWrong: We need a for loop that iterates through each character. Try: for (let right = 0; right < s.length; right++)

steps.title: Handle duplicates - shrink the window
steps.instruction: Inside the loop, check if the current character (s[right]) is already in charSet. If it is, we need to shrink the window by removing characters from the left until the duplicate is gone.
steps.hint: Use a while loop to remove s[left] from charSet and increment left while s[right] is in charSet.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! This handles the shrinking part of our sliding window.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good progress! Remember to check if the character exists, then remove from left.
steps.feedbackWrong: We need to shrink when we find a duplicate. Try: while (charSet.has(s[right])) { charSet.delete(s[left]); left++; }

steps.title: Expand the window and update max
steps.instruction: After handling duplicates, add the current character to charSet (expanding the window). Then calculate the current window size and update maxLength if needed.
steps.hint: Add s[right] to charSet, then calculate window size as right - left + 1.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! Now we're expanding the window and tracking the maximum size.
steps.feedbackPartial: Almost there! Don't forget to add the character to the Set and update maxLength.
steps.feedbackWrong: We need to add the character and update the maximum. Try: charSet.add(s[right]); maxLength = Math.max(maxLength, right - left + 1);

steps.title: Return the result
steps.instruction: Finally, return maxLength instead of 0. This completes our implementation!
steps.hint: Simply change the return statement to return maxLength.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Excellent! You've successfully implemented the sliding window algorithm!
steps.feedbackPartial: Close! Just need to return the correct variable.
steps.feedbackWrong: We should return maxLength, not 0. Change the return statement to return maxLength;

content.body: Congratulations! You've implemented the sliding window algorithm for finding the longest substring without repeating characters. Remember: the window expands when we see new unique characters, and shrinks from the left when we encounter duplicates. This efficient approach runs in O(n) time, much better than checking all possible substrings!
content.title: Done
